content.value_statement: Alembic autogenerate can create migrations that lose data or lock tables. This skill gives practical PostgreSQL patterns for safer schema changes, reviews, testing, and production rollout.
actual_capabilities: Explains common Alembic commands for revision generation, upgrades, downgrades, history, and branch heads.
Shows how to review autogenerated migrations for unsafe drop-and-add rename patterns.
Provides examples for non-nullable columns, data migrations, enum changes, indexes, and foreign keys.
Covers large-table concerns such as concurrent indexes, batching, and statement timeouts.
Includes a migration review checklist for downgrade coverage, naming, constraints, and testing.
Shows pytest-style migration upgrade and downgrade test patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not inspect a live database by itself.
Examples assume PostgreSQL and may need changes for other database engines.
It cannot verify production data volume, locks, or runtime permissions without project context.
It does not replace a human review before applying migrations to production.

use_cases.title: Review an autogenerated migration
use_cases.description: Check an Alembic autogenerate result for data-loss patterns, missing names, unsafe constraints, and incomplete downgrade logic.

use_cases.title: Plan a production schema change
use_cases.description: Design safer PostgreSQL steps for large tables, non-null columns, indexes, enum changes, and data backfills.

use_cases.title: Add migration tests to a service
use_cases.description: Create test coverage that upgrades, downgrades, and upgrades again to catch broken migration history early.

prompt_templates.title: Review my migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one migration file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Alembic migration for PostgreSQL safety. Check for data loss, missing downgrade steps, unsafe defaults, and lock risks. Explain the changes I should make.

prompt_templates.title: Create a safe migration plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning before writing a migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an Alembic migration for this schema change. Use PostgreSQL-safe steps, include downgrade behavior, and call out testing requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Fix autogenerated output
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced conversion from autogenerate to a safer migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: This Alembic autogenerate output looks risky. Rewrite the migration approach to preserve data, use explicit names, and handle existing rows safely.

prompt_templates.title: Assess production rollout risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this migration for production rollout. Consider locks, large-table behavior, concurrent indexes, enum changes, transaction settings, backups, and rollback options.

output_examples.input: A migration renames users.name to users.full_name but autogenerate produced a drop and add.
output_examples.output: The review flags data loss risk and recommends an explicit column rename. It also asks for a matching downgrade and a migration test.

output_examples.input: A new non-nullable role column must be added to a table that already has rows.
output_examples.output: The response proposes adding the column as nullable, backfilling existing rows, then applying the not-null constraint in a later step.

output_examples.input: A large events table needs a new index on user_id.
output_examples.output: The guidance recommends a concurrent index, autocommit considerations, downgrade handling, and a production review for lock behavior.

best_practices: Review every autogenerated migration before it reaches production.
Use explicit names for indexes, foreign keys, constraints, and enum types.
Test upgrade, downgrade, and upgrade again with realistic data where possible.
anti_patterns: Treating a column rename as drop and add without preserving existing data.
Adding a non-nullable column to a populated table without a backfill plan.
Applying production migrations without preview, backup, rollback, and lock review.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and review guidance. Any command execution requires the user or agent to run explicit commands.

faq.question: Which database does it target?
faq.answer: The examples target PostgreSQL with Alembic and SQLAlchemy. Other databases may need different migration patterns.

faq.question: Can it prevent all migration downtime?
faq.answer: No. It highlights safer patterns, but production risk depends on data size, indexes, locks, traffic, and deployment process.

faq.question: Does it cover data migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for backfills and transformations during schema changes.

faq.question: Can it help with multiple Alembic heads?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to detect multiple heads and create merge migrations.

faq.question: Is human review still required?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly treats migrations as high-risk changes that require review before deployment.
